findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the 271c characterization: 271c implements `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` delegating to `wiki_render.py` (a codec op DOES reference it) with a non-identity `normalize_outbound`; only the LIVE SEND wiring is deferred to 3388 — so state the boundary as 'codec op reference exists; live-send wiring is out of scope', not 'fully identity / not referenced by any codec op'.
evidence: Plan text: '271c leaves `WikiTextCodec` fully identity and delivers `wiki_render.py` as a pure module not referenced by any codec op or live send path in that story (271c\'s own words)'
271c description: 'Implement the segmenting renderer as **`WikiTextCodec.to_wire`** (delegating to a new `wiki_render.py` module)'
271c description: '`normalize_outbound(t)` = **`decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` by construction** (no longer identity)'
271c AC-1: '`WikiTextCodec.to_wire` segments a body and renders only structurally-safe units'
271c's actual OUT-of-scope list is only the live send wiring (outbound_mapper.py:77 and backend.py:70), not the codec-op reference
findings.finding: The plan asserts, attributing the words to 271c, that '271c leaves `WikiTextCodec` fully identity and delivers `wiki_render.py` as a pure module not referenced by any codec op ... in that story'. Reading prerequisite 271c refutes this: 271c implements the renderer AS `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` (delegating to `wiki_render.py`) and sets `normalize_outbound = decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` explicitly 'no longer identity'; its AC-1 is that `to_wire` segments and renders. Thus `wiki_render.py` IS referenced by the `to_wire` codec op in 271c, and the codec is not fully identity. Only the LIVE SEND wiring (outbound_mapper.py:77, backend.py:70) is deferred to 3388.
findings.location: Plan § 'Prior art / dependency boundaries', bullet 2 ('271c leaves `WikiTextCodec` fully identity ... (271c\'s own words)')
scenarios: An implementer trusts the 'fully identity / not referenced by any codec op' premise and assumes wiki_render.py has no caller, when in fact 271c's `to_wire` already calls it — hardening changes to wiki_render.py's function signatures/behavior must stay compatible with that existing `to_wire` call site.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: '271c wires `wiki_render.py` behind `WikiTextCodec.to_wire` (a non-identity codec op) but deliberately leaves the LIVE SEND sites (outbound_mapper.py:77, backend.py:70) on the plain/identity path; this story hardens the `wiki_render.py` functions reached via `to_wire` and touches neither the live send nor 3388\'s cutover.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace 'reuse the ACLI caller’s existing constants' with renderer-owned grace/drain constants defined in `wiki_render.py` (pandoc-appropriate, since ADR-0035 bars importing `adapters/jira`'s private ACLI constants and pandoc has no JVM-flush need), and name their values.
evidence: Plan: '`grace`/`drain` reuse the ACLI caller’s existing constants.'
`acli_subprocess.py:44-45`: `_ACLI_GRACE_SECONDS: int = 3  # ... JVM flush headroom`, `_ACLI_DRAIN_SECONDS: int = 2` — module-private, no export
`harness.py:120-125` defines its OWN `_GRACE_SECONDS`/`_DRAIN_SECONDS`; each caller pins its own constants — the shared `_proc.py` helper takes them as params, it does not own defaults
271c cites ADR-0035: 'jira_family/ must not import adapters/jira/' — so wiki_render.py cannot import the ACLI constants
The ACLI grace is 'JVM flush headroom'; pandoc has no JVM, so blind reuse is also semantically wrong-fit
findings.finding: The plan states the pandoc timeout's grace/drain values 'reuse the ACLI caller's existing constants', but those constants (`_ACLI_GRACE_SECONDS`, `_ACLI_DRAIN_SECONDS`) are module-private to `adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py`, which the renderer in `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` cannot import under ADR-0035/0055's vendor-adapter seam (jira_family must not import adapters/jira). No shared constants home exists (the grounding harness defines its own copy), so the reaper's kill timing — a load-bearing part of the timeout mechanism — cannot be sourced as the plan describes.
findings.location: Approach — 'Hard timeout + process-group reaping + batch-level verbatim fallback'
scenarios: Implementer tries `from ...adapters.jira.acli_subprocess import _ACLI_GRACE_SECONDS` and violates the vendor seam (or the constant is private and unimportable)
The renderer's actual kill timing is left unpinned because the named source of constants is inaccessible
findings.suggested_fix: State that wiki_render.py defines its own `_DC_PANDOC_GRACE_S`/`_DC_PANDOC_DRAIN_S` module constants passed to `reap_process_group(..., grace=, drain=, label="dc-pandoc", logger=...)`, rather than importing the private ACLI constants across the vendor seam.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the timeout + process-group reaping path behaves on Windows (does `reap_process_group` already gate POSIX-only `killpg`/`start_new_session`, is there a Windows fallback such as `TerminateProcess`/job objects, or is DC rendering documented as POSIX-only?), so the timeout guarantee is defined for the Windows platform cell.
evidence: Plan: 'builds its OWN subprocess.Popen([pandoc_path, …], start_new_session=True) … passes that Popen to the shared leaf rebar._proc.reap_process_group … killpg SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL'
Plan: 'the exact helper already reused by the ACLI transport and grounding harness' — indicates a pre-existing shared leaf whose Windows behavior is not re-specified here
Platform fact: os.killpg and process-group semantics are POSIX-only; on Windows start_new_session has no process-group effect and killpg is unavailable
findings.finding: The plan mandates `subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True)` plus process-group reaping via `rebar._proc.reap_process_group` (`killpg` SIGTERM→SIGKILL) as THE required timeout mechanism, but `start_new_session` and `os.killpg`/POSIX process groups do not exist on Windows; the plan does not state how the timeout+reap path behaves on the Windows platform cell of the support matrix.
findings.location: Approach → 'Hard timeout + process-group reaping' and AC line 1
scenarios: Platform=Windows (CI or developer workstation): a pandoc render that exceeds dc_pandoc_timeout_s reaches the reap path and either raises AttributeError (os.killpg absent) or fails to kill the spinning pandoc grandchild, so the pathological-hang hazard this story exists to fix is not mitigated on Windows and the reconcile can still stall.

evidence: Plan: 'feeds that run to pandoc as one Markdown document → one wiki segment ... there is no per-unit re-splitting of a batch’s output'
271c validated its guarantees per-unit and its AC asserts 'zero prose corruption ... verified by test_dc_corpus_coverage' on the per-unit pipeline
271c: 'render structurally-safe units ... reassemble in original order' — the corruption-free proof is at unit granularity, not run granularity
This story's Testing section asserts batching + order and spawn count but names no batching-equivalence assertion (combined render == concatenated per-unit renders)
findings.finding: The plan changes pandoc's input granularity from 271c's per-unit rendering to a per-safe-RUN combined Markdown document but does not establish that rendering a concatenated safe run is lossless/non-corrupting the way 271c validated per-unit rendering. Markdown block parsing is context-sensitive across unit boundaries (reference-style link definitions, list/paragraph adjacency, setext underlines), so a combined-run render is not guaranteed identical to concatenated per-unit renders — potentially re-introducing corruption at unit joins that 271c's per-unit path proved absent.
findings.location: Approach — 'Bound the per-render subprocess cost by batching contiguous SAFE units'
scenarios: A safe run where a reference-style link definition in one unit is consumed differently when adjacent prose is present in the same pandoc input
A list unit immediately followed by a paragraph unit whose jira output differs when rendered together vs. separately
